# Call-library dependencies

## `webrtc-sys` 0.3.48

`webrtc-sys-0.3.48` contains the build inputs of the published `webrtc-sys` 0.3.48 crate. The source archive has SHA-256 `9d87fa13acfe63505a0e8c1311b5dc60323a429196c4a7ba18b63de34e5cba67`. Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch and the standalone test participant's patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `src/`, `include/`, `README.md` and `NOTICE.md`. The archive's development instructions, changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest, native-library build scripts and unused native tests are not required by this build and are omitted. Copyright and licence notices in the retained inputs are unchanged.

The peer-connection destructor in `src/peer_connection.cpp` calls `Close` while both its native interface and observer still exist. Linux runtime initialization also registers a system-root TLS verifier from `src/system_certificate_verifier.{rs,cpp}` through the pinned binary's platform-verifier API. It uses `rustls-native-certs` to load roots and Rustls to verify chains with SSL server purpose. The build adds that bridge and its Rust dependencies only on Linux. Every throw of the crate throws `livekit_ffi::Exception` of `include/livekit/exception.h`, which owns its message; the WebRTC library for Windows, whose defines the crate uses, has `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0`, and with that value `std::runtime_error` keeps only a pointer to its message. The same header gives each bridge with a C++ function that returns `Result` its catch (`rust::behavior::trycatch`): an exception of the crate becomes a Rust error, and any other C++ exception ends the process with a line on standard error, written from a buffer on the stack to the handle of standard error, without an allocation and without the lock of the stream `stderr`, and followed by a line of readable names, after the Windows message box of `abort()` has been turned off; `src/exception.rs` also has test functions that hold that lock and that throw a subclass of `std::exception`. `src/exception.rs` with `src/exception.cpp` are a bridge of test functions for it. The audio processing module of `include/livekit/apm.h` processes at 48 kHz inside: the default of the WebRTC version is 32 kHz, at which the module resamples the stream of 48 kHz on the way in and out and removes everything above 16 kHz. `include/livekit/yuv_helper.h` and `src/yuv_helper.rs` add `i420_scale`, the scale of the published `I420Buffer::scale` with planes that the caller holds and does not give up, so that a received picture is scaled without a copy of its planes. `src/video_encoder_factory.cpp` and `include/livekit/video_encoder_factory.h` make every encoder through `CreateAdaptedEncoder`, which gives the simulcast adapter of WebRTC a factory of the software encoders for a format of a hardware backend, so that a hardware encoder that does not start or fails is replaced by the software encoder of its codec; `src/encoder_fallback.rs`, `src/encoder_fallback.cpp` and `include/livekit/encoder_fallback.h` are a bridge of a test function for it. ADR 0733 explains the six corrections, their regression checks and the combined compiled-in/system trust policy. The WebRTC binary revision and every other dependency version are unchanged.

Each changed source file states in its header that it differs from the published version, and each change carries a `Modified:` comment; a new file states that it is not in the published crate. `Cargo.toml` carries its `Modified:` comment above the added dependencies.

Remove the destructor correction when the pinned upstream crate closes its native peer connection before releasing these members. Remove the Linux trust correction when a pinned upstream version provides system-root verification for every default TLS adapter. Remove the exception correction when a pinned upstream version throws only exceptions that own their message, also with `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0`, and its bridges end the process at every other C++ exception. Remove the processing rate when the default of the pinned WebRTC version is 48 kHz or a pinned upstream version sets it, the scale when a pinned upstream version scales planes that it reads only, and the software fallback when a pinned upstream version gives the simulcast adapter a software fallback. Run the native destruction tests, window live tier and media live tier when replacing this dependency; the Linux media live tier includes the TURN TLS trust regression. Run `crates/media/tests/native_exceptions.rs` and the three exception tests of `engine::tests` (ADR 0733) on Windows when replacing this dependency or the WebRTC binary. Run `audio::processing::tests::the_module_keeps_the_microphone_above_16_khz`, `share::picture::tests::held_planes_are_scaled_as_the_call_library_scales_them` and the test target `encoder_fallback` of `junto-media` when replacing it.

## `webrtc-sys-build` 0.3.19

`webrtc-sys-build-0.3.19` contains the build inputs of the published `webrtc-sys-build` 0.3.19 crate, the build-script helper of `webrtc-sys` that downloads and extracts the WebRTC library. The source archive has SHA-256 `0cd4f418e16f4b7ba028e6b5c70e4f532c7d2b5ca39726d42b699f3e4591ed5c`, the checksum that the lockfile held for the registry version. The archive was made from commit `2d9f01ab1e933a86a8a5c53805ee29ee58b9be1b` of the upstream repository, directory `webrtc-sys/build` (its `.cargo_vcs_info.json`). Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch and the standalone test participant's patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml` and `src/`. The archive's changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` are not required by this build and are omitted. The archive has no separate licence file; the crate is licensed under Apache-2.0 (its manifest), and the copyright and licence notice at the top of `src/lib.rs` is unchanged.

`src/lib.rs` is unchanged. `Cargo.toml` differs in one dependency, marked with a `Modified:` comment: `zip` 9.0.4 with its deflate decompressor (`deflate-flate2-zlib-rs`) replaces `zip` 0.6 with the feature `deflate`. The `ZipArchive::extract` of `zip` 0.6 keeps the setuid, setgid and sticky bits of an entry (RUSTSEC-2026-0367) and applies permissions through extracted symbolic links (RUSTSEC-2026-0369). ADR 0733 explains the correction and its checks. Every other dependency version is unchanged.

Remove this copy when a pinned upstream version depends on `zip` 9.0.0 or later. Build `junto-media` from an empty build directory on macOS and Linux when replacing it, so that the WebRTC archive is downloaded and extracted again, then run `cargo deny check` and the media live tier.

## `livekit` 0.9.4

`livekit-0.9.4` contains the build inputs of the published `livekit` 0.9.4 crate. The source archive has SHA-256 `4dc818741891a8179eafd4665156482761d5084fb15238c1de9c211fdb974e3e`, the checksum that the lockfile held for the registry version. The archive was made from commit `a6f93a16fa71fe811d040de175e070e233d9b1fe` of the upstream repository, directory `livekit` (its `.cargo_vcs_info.json`). Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch and the standalone test participant's patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `src/` and `README.md`. The archive's changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, examples, specifications and tests are not required by this build and are omitted. The archive has no separate licence file; the crate is licensed under Apache-2.0 (its manifest), and the copyright and licence notice at the top of each retained source file is unchanged.

Every file and every dependency version not named below are unchanged. Each changed file states in its header that it differs from the published version, and each change carries a `Modified:` comment; a new file states that it is not in the published crate. ADR 0733 explains each correction and its regression checks. Remove a correction when a pinned upstream version makes it unnecessary, and remove this copy when no correction remains. Run the tests of each remaining correction against a new version first, then the window live tier and the media live tier.

Corrections:

- Publisher negotiation queue. `src/rtc_engine/negotiation_queue.rs` is new; `src/rtc_engine/mod.rs` and `src/rtc_engine/rtc_session.rs` use it. The queue of the fast publish mode decides with one state under one lock whether a task negotiates. The published version also kept a separate flag for a running task; a request that came after the task had set the state to idle and before it cleared that flag was dropped, and every later request with it. `crates/media/tests/negotiation_queue.rs` compiles the new file and runs its tests in the workspace suite. Removed when a pinned upstream version decides the queue under one state, so that a request after the end of a negotiation always starts another one.
- Order of mute requests. `src/room/participant/in_order.rs` is new; `src/room/participant/mod.rs` uses it. The mute and unmute requests of the local tracks of a participant are sent one after the other, in the order of the changes. The published version started a task for each request; tasks that waited together for a restored connection sent in any order, and a mute that reached the media server after the unmute that followed it left the track muted there. `crates/media/tests/mute_order.rs` compiles the new file and runs its tests in the workspace suite, and reads the source of `src/room/participant/mod.rs` to check that every mute request of the participant goes through it. Removed when a pinned upstream version sends the mute requests of a track in their order.
- Mute state after a resume. `src/room/participant/mod.rs`, `src/room/participant/local_participant.rs` and `src/room/mod.rs`: after each resume of the session the participant sends the mute state of each local track again, after the mute requests given before. The published version sent nothing; a mute request written to a lost signal connection before the loss was found reaches the media server late or not at all, the media server discards it when it arrives after the resume, and it does not take the mute state from the resume. The resume carries the mute flag of each publication at the time of publishing, because the SDK does not update the publication information of a local track after the publish. `crates/media/tests/mute_order.rs` reads the source of `src/room/mod.rs`, `src/room/participant/local_participant.rs` and `src/room/participant/mod.rs` to check that the room sends the mute states after each resume and that each request reads the state in its turn; the media live test `sound::an_open_written_to_a_lost_signal_connection_reaches_the_media_server_after_the_resume` checks the result with a media server. Removed when a pinned upstream version sends the current mute state after a resume, or when a pinned upstream version updates the publication information that the resume sends at each mute change and the pinned media server takes the mute state from the resume.
- Negotiation after the close. `src/room/mod.rs`, `src/rtc_engine/mod.rs` and `src/rtc_engine/rtc_session.rs`: the close of a room calls `RtcEngine::begin_close` before it unpublishes the tracks, and from then on the session starts no negotiation of the publisher; the close ends a wait for an answer, and `offer_publisher` makes no offer in a session that closes and takes an offer whose result comes after the close began as the end of the negotiation, with a debug line. The published version negotiated for each unpublished track while the room closed: it waited 10 seconds for an answer of a closed session, logged "peer connection is closed, cannot create offer", or logged the error "Failed to set local offer sdp: Called in wrong state: closed". The media live test `close::a_leave_starts_no_negotiation_of_the_publisher` leaves a call with two published tracks while it holds the media server alone with one person in the room, and counts the negotiations that the leaves start, the failed negotiations and the offers in a closed connection. Removed when a pinned upstream version does not negotiate the publisher of a room that closes.
